 Hong Kong Open: Teen Santhosh Ramraj Shocks Idol Chen
 Thursday, November 19, 2026
 TEXT BY PREM KUMAR | TAN EN EN/BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Never meet your heroes, unless you are 19-year-old Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj , in which case you might just knock them out of a Super 500 tournament.
 The Indian world No.47 delivered the shock of LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Thursday, toppling pre-tournament favourite and world No.4 Chen Yu Fei 21-18 24-22 in the second round.
 Just 24 hours after banking her maiden top 20 scalp against Mia Blichfeldt, Santhosh Ramraj bagged her first top 10 victory – becoming the first player outside the top 30 to beat Chen since Gregoria Mariska Tunjung in 2017.
 “She’s my biggest idol and I still can’t believe I won against her,” Santhosh Ramraj admitted afterward, visibly awestruck. “This will be one of the most memorable days in my playing career.”
 The win was no fluke. Combining fearless aggression with stubborn defence, Santhosh Ramraj refused to blink even when staring down a 15-5 deficit in the second game. Ironically, her secret weapon was simply mentally clocking in for a decider.
 “Actually, I was preparing for the third game,” she laughed. “I just didn’t want to give up so easily. Since she’s so senior, I had nothing to lose, so I kept on trying. It worked out really well that I was able to close the gap.”
 Behind the giantkilling performance lies a quiet story of family sacrifice. Six years ago, her family uprooted their lives in Coimbatore and moved to Hyderabad so she could train at the Gopichand Academy – a leap of faith now paying dividends. Having reached the Korea Masters semifinals in August, she is now into her first Super 500 quarterfinal of the season.
 “I think I’m not less than anyone,” she said, the awe quickly giving way to conviction. “I’m very thankful to all my coaches for supporting me throughout this journey.”
 Her reward for slaying her idol? A maiden clash with Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong, who swept Lin Hsiang Ti 21-11 21-12 to keep her HSBC BWF World Tour Finals hopes alive.
 If Thursday proved anything, Chochuwong shouldn’t expect the teenager to show too much respect.

 WHAT OTHERS SAID 
 “I can’t find the words. It was a difficult match but I did it. This is a very meaningful moment as I got a breakthrough.” – Zhu Xuan Chen after beating Lin Chun-Yi to reach his first Super 500 quarterfinal
 “We are not thinking about Hangzhou at all. We are more focused on getting back our rhythm and confidence. Perhaps that’s why we’ve been able to play without pressure.” – Shevon Jemie Lai, who with Goh Soon Huat, are one of two pairs vying for the last available spot at the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals
 Zhu takes on Anders Antonsen in the last eight.
